name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent on every pull request before human review. It catches 80% of trivia like typos, formatting, and missing docs, freeing humans for real decisions. The trade-off is setup time—configuring PR-Agent and training the team—but the net gain is faster, cleaner merges.

name: Gauge
text: PR-Agent’s false positives aren’t the only risk—it also misses context-dependent issues like architectural drift or security gaps, where 20% of the misses matter more than the 80% trivia it catches. A better alternative is to use PR-Agent as a *filter*, not a gatekeeper: run it post-review to clean up trivia, but keep humans in the loop for decisions where context and trade-offs matter. Settle it by measuring how often PR-Agent’s misses force reverts or post-merge fixes in the next two sprints.
